example.fact: Major Chinese flower expos, especially in Yunnan province, have helped make the region one of the largest cut-flower production centers in Asia, exporting millions of stems daily.

components.note: 阝 (mound/place) — on the left side, a form of 阜 (mound, earthworks), often relating to terrain, elevation, or place.
遂 (suí, also suì) gives the sound — an exact match with 隧's reading.

example.hanzi: 汽车穿过一条长长的隧道。
example.pinyin: Qìchē chuānguò yì tiáo chángcháng de suìdào.
example.english: The car passes through a long tunnel.
example.fact: The Channel Tunnel connecting England and France runs about 50 kilometers, with roughly 38 km under the seabed itself, making it one of the longest undersea tunnels in the world.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — the grass/plant radical, marking the character as related to plants or vegetation.
耳 (ěr) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer closely matches 茸's reading rōng.

example.hanzi: 鹿茸在中药里被认为很珍贵。
example.pinyin: Lùrōng zài zhōngyào lǐ bèi rènwéi hěn zhēnguì.
example.english: Velvet antler is considered very precious in traditional Chinese medicine.
example.fact: Deer antler velvet is the soft, developing antler tissue harvested before it hardens into bone, and it's one of the fastest-growing tissues in the animal kingdom, growing over a centimeter per day during peak season.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — the metal radical, marking the character as related to metal or metalworking.
甘 (gān) gives a sound close to 钳's reading qián, sharing the same rhyme core -an.

example.hanzi: 他用钳子拔出了钉子。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng qiánzi báchūle dīngzi.
example.english: He used pliers to pull out the nail.
example.fact: Many crustaceans, like crabs and lobsters, have claws that function like a natural pair of pliers — the coconut crab in particular has one of the strongest pinching forces relative to body size of any animal on Earth.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the mouth radical, marking the character as related to speech, sound, or an action of the mouth.
肯 (kěn) gives the sound — an exact match with 啃's reading.

example.hanzi: 小狗在啃骨头。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu zài kěn gǔtou.
example.english: The puppy is gnawing on a bone.
example.fact: 啃老 (literally 'to gnaw on the old') is modern Chinese slang for adult children who remain financially dependent on their aging parents, a phenomenon that has drawn significant social discussion in China.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the person radical, marking the character as describing a person, their role, or their behavior.
牙 (yá) gives the sound — an exact match with 伢's reading.

example.hanzi: 武汉话里，'伢'是'小孩'的意思。
example.pinyin: Wǔhànhuà lǐ, 'yá' shì 'xiǎohái' de yìsi.
example.english: In the Wuhan dialect, 'yá' means 'child.'
example.fact: 伢 is a common dialect word for 'child' across parts of central China, including Wuhan and Changsha, where a young kid might affectionately be called 小伢.

components.note: 门 (gate/door) — depicts a double door or gate, marking the character as related to doors, gates, or enclosures.
圭 (guī) gives the sound — an exact match with 闺's reading.

example.hanzi: 她和闺蜜一起逛街。
example.pinyin: Tā hé guīmì yīqǐ guàngjiē.
example.english: She goes shopping with her close female friend.
example.fact: 闺蜜, literally 'boudoir-close [friend],' has become one of the most common modern Chinese terms for a close female friend, especially popularized through social media and entertainment in the 2000s and 2010s.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — depicts a tongue, marking the character as related to the mouth or speech.
忝 (tiǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 舔's reading.

example.hanzi: 小狗舔了舔主人的手。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu tiǎnle tiǎn zhǔrén de shǒu.
example.english: The puppy licked its owner's hand.
example.fact: A dog's tongue has far fewer taste buds than a human's, roughly 1,700 versus about 9,000, which is part of why dogs rely so heavily on smell rather than taste to explore the world.

meanings: to step on; to tread on
to put on; to wear (shoes, trousers etc)

components.note: 足 (foot) — the foot radical, marking the character as related to the foot, legs, or walking.
登 (dēng) gives the sound — an exact match with 蹬's reading.

example.hanzi: 他用力蹬着自行车上坡。
example.pinyin: Tā yònglì dēngzhe zìxíngchē shàng pō.
example.english: He pedaled the bicycle hard up the slope.
example.fact: The pedal-and-crank bicycle mechanism, which turns a downward push of the leg into rotational motion, was refined into essentially its modern form by the 1880s with the 'safety bicycle.'

meanings: (bound form) (of muscles) to cramp; to spasm

components.note: 手 (hand) — depicts a hand, marking the character as related to actions done by hand.

example.hanzi: 他的腿突然痉挛了一下。
example.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ tūrán jìngluánle yíxià.
example.english: His leg suddenly cramped up.
example.fact: Muscle cramps are often caused by a combination of dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, and muscle fatigue, which is why athletes are advised to replenish electrolytes, not just water, during intense exercise.

components.note: 目 (eye) — the eye radical, marking the character as related to sight or the eyes.
兆 (zhào) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer closely matches 眺's reading tiào.

example.hanzi: 站在山顶可以眺望整个城市。
example.pinyin: Zhàn zài shāndǐng kěyǐ tiàowàng zhěnggè chéngshì.
example.english: Standing on the mountaintop, you can gaze out over the entire city.
example.fact: 远眺 ('gazing far into the distance') is frequently recommended in Chinese eye-health advice as a way to relax eye focusing muscles after prolonged close-up screen use.

meanings: a piece of cloth used wrap bundles
(bound form) a cloth used to wrap or cover
etymologyHint: Something wrapped 伏 in cloth 衤; 伏 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 衤 (clothing) marks this character as related to cloth or fabric.
伏 means 'to lie prostrate, to hide' and is pronounced fú — identical to 袱 — combined with 'cloth,' evoking something wrapped and concealed within fabric, as in 包袱 (bāofu, 'a cloth-wrapped bundle').

example.hanzi: 别把过去的失败当成包袱。
example.pinyin: Bié bǎ guòqù de shībài dàngchéng bāofu.
example.english: Don't treat past failures as a burden weighing you down.
example.fact: 包袱 also has a specialized meaning in traditional Chinese comedic performance (相声, crosstalk), where it refers to a joke's setup and punchline — 'to shake open the bundle' means to deliver the punchline.

meanings: short name for Gansu 甘肅|甘肃[Gan1 su4]

components.note: 阝 (mound/place) — on the left side, a form of 阜 (mound, earthworks), often relating to terrain, elevation, or place.
龙 (lóng) gives a sound close to 陇's reading lǒng — the same syllable, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 陇海铁路连接着中国东西部。
example.pinyin: Lǒnghǎi Tiělù liánjiēzhe Zhōngguó dōngxībù.
example.english: The Longhai Railway connects eastern and western China.
example.fact: The idiom 得陇望蜀 ('having gained Long, one covets Shu') describes insatiable ambition. It comes from a letter the Han-dynasty Emperor Guangwu sent to his general after the general conquered the Long region (Gansu), urging him to press on and take Shu (Sichuan) too.

components.note: 殳 (weapon/tool) — depicts a hand wielding a weapon or pole-arm, marking the character as related to striking.
区 here carries the rare surname reading Ōu, giving the sound — an exact match with 殴's reading.

example.hanzi: 他因殴打他人被警方拘留。
example.pinyin: Tā yīn ōudǎ tārén bèi jǐngfāng jūliú.
example.english: He was detained by police for assaulting someone.
example.fact: 殴打 (assault/battery) is a specific term in Chinese criminal and civil law, distinguished from more serious charges based on the severity of the injury inflicted.

components.note: 木 (tree/wood) — the tree/wood radical, marking the character as related to trees, wood, or wooden objects.
市 (shì) gives the sound — an exact match with 柿's reading.

example.hanzi: 秋天，树上挂满了红红的柿子。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān, shù shàng guà mǎnle hónghóng de shìzi.
example.english: In autumn, the tree is covered with red persimmons.
example.fact: Unripe persimmons contain high levels of tannins that make them intensely astringent and almost inedible, but the fruit turns sweet once fully ripened or processed by drying, freezing, or exposure to ethylene gas.

components.note: 木 (tree/wood) — the tree/wood radical, marking the character as related to trees, wood, or wooden objects.
吾 (wú) gives the sound — an exact match with 梧's reading.

example.hanzi: 院子里种着一棵梧桐树。
example.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ zhòngzhe yì kē wútóngshù.
example.english: A Chinese parasol tree is planted in the courtyard.
example.fact: In Chinese folklore, the legendary phoenix is said to perch only on the wutong tree (梧桐), making it a traditional symbol of nobility often planted near scholars' homes and imperial gardens.

meanings: (literary) to come to one's senses; to awaken
etymologyHint: A brilliant 星 mind 忄; 星 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) shows the character relates to mental clarity or awareness.

星 means 'star' and is pronounced xīng — identical to 惺 — evoking a mind as clear as a bright star, giving 惺 its meaning 'clever, alert,' as in 惺忪 (xīngsōng, bleary-eyed on waking) or 惺惺 (xīngxīng, astute).

example.hanzi: 他睡眼惺忪地走出房间。
example.pinyin: Tā shuìyǎn xīngsōng de zǒuchū fángjiān.
example.english: He walked out of the room, bleary-eyed from sleep.
example.fact: 惺忪 is one of many Chinese descriptive binomes built from two rhyming syllables for their evocative sound rather than separable meaning, much like English 'mumbo-jumbo.'

components.note: 弓 (bow) — depicts a bow (the weapon), marking the character as related to bows or their action.
也 (yě) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer closely matches 弛's reading chí.

example.hanzi: 做完瑜伽后，他感觉全身松弛。
example.pinyin: Zuò wán yújiā hòu, tā gǎnjué quánshēn sōngchí.
example.english: After finishing yoga, he felt completely relaxed all over.
example.fact: The idiom 一张一弛 ('alternating tension and relaxation') comes from the Confucian Book of Rites, which compares good rule to properly tensioning and loosening a bow.

meanings: used in 僬僥|僬侥[jiao1 yao2]

components.note: 亻 (person) — the person radical, marking the character as describing a person, their role, or their behavior.
尧 (yáo) gives a sound close to 侥's reading jiǎo — they share the same rhyme core -ao.

example.hanzi: 他侥幸逃过了这次考试的处罚。
example.pinyin: Tā jiǎoxìng táoguòle zhè cì kǎoshì de chǔfá.
example.english: He luckily escaped punishment for this exam by sheer chance.
example.fact: 侥幸心理 ('lucky-chance mentality') is a common term in Chinese safety education, describing the risky mindset of people who break rules assuming they won't get caught.

components.note: 王 (jade) — a form of 玉 (jade), marking the character as related to jade or a precious stone.
罙 (a rare component, historically read close to shēn) gives a sound close to 琛's reading chēn, sharing the same final, with initials sh/ch differing only in retroflex quality.

example.hanzi: 琛这个字常用来给孩子取名，寓意像珍宝一样珍贵。
example.pinyin: Chēn zhège zì cháng yòng lái gěi háizi qǔmíng, yùyì xiàng zhēnbǎo yīyàng zhēnguì.
example.english: The character 'chēn' is often used in children's names, symbolizing something as precious as a treasure.
example.fact: 琛 combines the 'jade' component 王 with a phonetic element, and because it means 'treasure, precious stone,' it remains popular in Chinese given names even though it's rarely used in everyday vocabulary otherwise.

meanings: to give (sb) a nudge; to prod

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the hand radical, marking the character as related to an action performed with the hand.
甬 (yǒng) gives a sound close to 捅's reading tǒng, sharing the same final -ong.

example.hanzi: 他不小心捅了个大麻烦。
example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn tǒngle gè dà máfan.
example.english: He carelessly stirred up a big problem.
example.fact: The colloquial phrase 捅马蜂窝 ('to poke a hornet's nest') is a vivid Chinese idiom for provoking serious trouble, much like the English 'to open a can of worms.'

components.note: 酉 (wine vessel) — depicts a wine jar, marking the character as related to alcohol or fermentation.
云 (yún) gives a sound close to 酝's reading yùn — the same syllable, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这项计划已经酝酿了很久。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng jìhuà yǐjīng yùnniàngle hěn jiǔ.
example.english: This plan has been brewing/in the works for a long time.
example.fact: 酝酿 originally described the literal fermentation of brewing wine, and it became one of the most common Chinese metaphors for ideas or plans slowly developing before finally emerging.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — the grass/plant radical, marking the character as related to plants or vegetation.
署 (shǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 薯's reading.

example.hanzi: 冬天烤番薯特别好吃。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān kǎo fānshǔ tèbié hàochī.
example.english: Roasted sweet potatoes are especially delicious in winter.
example.fact: The sweet potato was introduced to China from the Americas in the late 16th century and became a crucial famine-resistant crop credited with helping sustain population growth during the Ming and Qing dynasties.

example.hanzi: 拖船在水面上拖曳着货船。
example.pinyin: Tuōchuán zài shuǐmiàn shàng tuōyèzhe huòchuán.
example.english: The tugboat tows the cargo ship across the water.
example.fact: 曳光弹 (tracer ammunition) contains a small pyrotechnic charge that burns brightly in flight, letting shooters visually track a bullet's trajectory — the same 'trailing' idea 曳 conveys.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water radical, marking the character as related to water or liquid.

example.hanzi: 溪水清澈见底。
example.pinyin: Xīshuǐ qīngchè jiàndǐ.
example.english: The stream water is so clear you can see the bottom.
example.fact: Crater Lake in Oregon, formed from a collapsed volcano about 7,700 years ago, is renowned as one of the clearest and deepest lakes in the world, with visibility sometimes exceeding 30 meters.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — the metal radical, marking the character as related to metal or metalworking.
秀 (xiù) gives the sound — an exact match with 锈's reading.

example.hanzi: 这把旧刀已经生锈了。
example.pinyin: Zhè bǎ jiù dāo yǐjīng shēngxiù le.
example.english: This old knife has already rusted.
example.fact: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and moisture in the air — the Statue of Liberty's copper skin, by contrast, doesn't rust this way but develops its own protective greenish patina through a different chemical process.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — the grain radical, depicting a stalk of grain, marking the character as related to crops or cereals.
周 (zhōu) gives a sound close to 稠's reading chóu, sharing the same final, with initials zh/ch differing only in aspiration.

example.hanzi: 这碗汤很浓稠。
example.pinyin: Zhè wǎn tāng hěn nóngchóu.
example.english: This bowl of soup is very thick.
example.fact: Honey is an unusually viscous liquid because of its extremely high sugar concentration and low water content, which is also why properly stored honey can remain edible for years, even centuries.

components.note: 目 (eye) — the eye radical, marking the character as related to sight or the eyes.
牟 (móu) gives the sound — an exact match with 眸's reading.

example.hanzi: 她有一双明亮的眸子。
example.pinyin: Tā yǒu yì shuāng míngliàng de móuzi.
example.english: She has a pair of bright, clear eyes.
example.fact: 眸 is a distinctly literary, poetic word for 'eye,' used almost exclusively in writing rather than everyday speech, where the plain word 眼睛 is used instead.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the mouth radical, marking the character as related to speech, sound, or an action of the mouth.
包 (bāo) gives a sound close to 咆's reading páo, sharing the same final, with initials b/p differing only in aspiration.

example.hanzi: 狮子在草原上咆哮。
example.pinyin: Shīzi zài cǎoyuán shàng páoxiào.
example.english: The lion roars on the grassland.
example.fact: A lion's roar can be heard from up to 8 kilometers away under the right conditions, thanks to a specialized flat, square-shaped vocal fold structure in its larynx.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — the bamboo radical, marking the character as related to bamboo or objects made of it.
黄 (huáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 簧's reading.

example.hanzi: 这个装置里有一个弹簧。
example.pinyin: Zhège zhuāngzhì lǐ yǒu yí gè tánhuáng.
example.english: There is a spring/coil inside this device.
example.fact: 簧 originally referred to the vibrating reed inside traditional wind instruments like the sheng (笙); the mechanical sense 'spring/coil' developed later by comparing a coiled spring's motion to a vibrating reed.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — depicts a bird, marking the character as related to birds.
区 here carries the rare surname reading Ōu, giving the sound — an exact match with 鸥's reading.

example.hanzi: 海边有很多海鸥在飞。
example.pinyin: Hǎibiān yǒu hěn duō hǎi'ōu zài fēi.
example.english: There are many seagulls flying by the seaside.
example.fact: Seagulls have specialized glands above their eyes that filter and excrete excess salt from seawater they ingest, letting them survive far from fresh water.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — the sickness radical, depicting a person lying on a sickbed — marking the character as related to illness.
昜 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 疡's reading; 昜 is the ancestor form behind 阳.

example.hanzi: 医生诊断他患有胃溃疡。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng zhěnduàn tā huànyǒu wèikuìyáng.
example.english: The doctor diagnosed him with a stomach ulcer.
example.fact: Stomach ulcers were long believed to be caused mainly by stress and diet, until scientists Barry Marshall and Robin Warren proved in the 1980s that the bacterium Helicobacter pylori was a primary cause, winning the 2005 Nobel Prize in Medicine.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water radical, marking the character as related to water or liquid.
卖 (mài) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer closely matches 渎's reading dú.

example.hanzi: 这名官员因渎职被处分。
example.pinyin: Zhè míng guānyuán yīn dúzhí bèi chǔfèn.
example.english: This official was disciplined for dereliction of duty.
example.fact: 渎职罪 (the crime of dereliction of duty) is a specific charge in Chinese criminal law applied to state officials who cause serious harm to public interests through negligence or abuse of their position.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water radical, marking the character as related to water or liquid.
及 (jí) gives the sound — an exact match with 汲's reading.

example.hanzi: 我们要从历史中汲取教训。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào cóng lìshǐ zhōng jíqǔ jiàoxùn.
example.english: We must draw lessons from history.
example.fact: 汲取 originally described the literal act of drawing water from a well with a rope and bucket, and it became one of the most common Chinese verbs for metaphorically 'absorbing' knowledge or lessons.

meanings: (literary) to amuse oneself; to play; to have fun

components.note: 女 (woman) — the woman radical, marking the character as related to a woman or a feminine quality.
喜 (xǐ) gives a sound close to 嬉's reading xī — the same syllable, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在公园里嬉戏玩耍。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài gōngyuán lǐ xīxì wánshuǎ.
example.english: The children play and frolic in the park.
example.fact: The English word 'hippie' was sometimes transliterated into 1960s-70s Chinese as 嬉皮, reusing this character 嬉 ('to play') purely for its sound while also hinting at the countercultural, playful lifestyle.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — a form of 肉 (flesh, body), marking the character as related to a body part or bodily substance.
农 (nóng) gives the sound — an exact match with 脓's reading.

example.hanzi: 伤口感染后开始化脓。
example.pinyin: Shāngkǒu gǎnrǎn hòu kāishǐ huànóng.
example.english: After the wound got infected, it began to fester.
example.fact: Pus is mainly composed of dead white blood cells, bacteria, and tissue debris — its characteristic yellowish-green color often comes from an enzyme released by the white blood cells fighting the infection.

components.note: 马 (horse) — depicts a horse, marking the character as related to horses.
累 (lèi, also léi/lěi) gives a sound close to 骡's reading luó, sharing the same initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 骡子既能驮东西，又很能吃苦。
example.pinyin: Luózi jì néng tuó dōngxi, yòu hěn néng chīkǔ.
example.english: Mules can both carry loads and endure hardship well.
example.fact: A mule is a hybrid offspring of a male donkey and a female horse, and mules are almost always sterile because their parent species have different numbers of chromosomes.

meanings: abbr. for Guangzhou 廣州|广州[Guang3 zhou1]

components.note: 禾 (grain) — the grain radical, depicting a stalk of grain, marking the character as related to crops or cereals.
惠 (huì) gives a sound close to 穗's reading suì, sharing the same final.

example.hanzi: 秋天，稻穗沉甸甸地低垂着。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān, dàosuì chéndiàndiàn de dīchuízhe.
example.english: In autumn, the heavy ears of rice hang low.
example.fact: 穗 is also the traditional one-character abbreviation for the city of Guangzhou, whose nickname is 'Rice-Ear City' (穗城).

meanings: to transport caged prisoner on a cart

components.note: 木 (tree/wood) — the tree/wood radical, marking the character as related to trees, wood, or wooden objects.
监 (jiān) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer closely matches 槛's reading kǎn.

example.hanzi: 这个行业的门槛很高。
example.pinyin: Zhège hángyè de ménkǎn hěn gāo.
example.english: The barrier to entry for this industry is very high.
example.fact: 门槛 is widely used metaphorically in modern Chinese to describe the minimum requirements or 'barrier to entry' for a job or opportunity, much like the English phrase 'a high bar to clear.'

meanings: to lift up; to carry in one's hand

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the hand radical, marking the character as related to an action performed with the hand.
令 (lìng) gives a sound close to 拎's reading līn, sharing the same initial and a similar nasal final.

example.hanzi: 她手里拎着一个大包。
example.pinyin: Tā shǒu lǐ līnzhe yí gè dà bāo.
example.english: She is carrying a big bag in her hand.
example.fact: 拎清楚 ('to carry clearly,' i.e. to think something through) is Shanghainese-influenced Mandarin slang that extends the physical image of 'carrying' something to sorting out a situation mentally.

example.hanzi: 巳时对应现在的上午九点到十一点。
example.pinyin: Sìshí duìyìng xiànzài de shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn dào shíyī diǎn.
example.english: The 'si' hour corresponds to today's 9 to 11 in the morning.
example.fact: 巳 is the sixth of the twelve Earthly Branches used in the traditional Chinese calendar system, and it corresponds to the Snake in the Chinese zodiac.

components.note: 阝 here is a form of 邑 (city, settlement) — unlike the more common left-side 阝 (from 阜, 'mound'), this one marks 邢 as a place name.

开 (kāi) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer closely matches 邢's reading xíng — the shape here likely descends from a separate ancient component (幵) that later merged visually with 开.

example.hanzi: 邢台是河北省的一座城市。
example.pinyin: Xíngtái shì Héběi Shěng de yí zuò chéngshì.
example.english: Xingtai is a city in Hebei province.
example.fact: Xingtai (邢台) is one of the oldest cities in China, with a history stretching back over 3,500 years, traditionally considered one of the early capitals during the Shang dynasty period.

etymologyHint: Two tens 十 side by side

components.note: 廿 is formed by fusing two 十 (ten) shapes together into a single stroke pattern, directly representing the number 'twenty' — the same principle used in 卅 (sà, 'thirty'), which fuses three 十 together.

example.hanzi: 今天是农历廿三。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān shì nónglì niànsān.
example.english: Today is the 23rd day of the lunar month.
example.fact: 廿 ('twenty') is still commonly used in Cantonese and on traditional lunar calendars — as in 年廿九, 'the 29th of the [lunar] year,' a common date for Lunar New Year's Eve — even though it's largely dropped out of everyday Mandarin.

meanings: to take by the arm and assist

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the hand radical, marking the character as related to an action performed with the hand.

example.hanzi: 他搀扶着年迈的奶奶过马路。
example.pinyin: Tā chānfúzhe niánmài de nǎinai guò mǎlù.
example.english: He supported his elderly grandmother by the arm across the street.
example.fact: 搀扶 is a common word in Chinese public-etiquette campaigns encouraging young people to assist elderly pedestrians, especially in crossing streets or navigating stairs.

components.note: 日 (sun) — depicts the sun, marking the character as related to daylight, time, or brightness.
署 (shǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 曙's reading.

example.hanzi: 经过多年努力，事情终于出现了曙光。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò duōnián nǔlì, shìqing zhōngyú chūxiànle shǔguāng.
example.english: After years of effort, a glimmer of hope finally appeared for the matter.
example.fact: 曙光 is often used metaphorically in Chinese to describe the first sign of hope after a long struggle, much like the English phrase 'a light at the end of the tunnel.'

etymologyHint: Wood 木 for burning 焦; 焦 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 木 (wood/tree) marks the character as related to trees or timber.
焦 means 'scorched, burnt' and is pronounced jiāo, close to (though not identical to) 樵's qiáo — evoking wood gathered for burning, giving 樵 its meaning 'firewood, woodcutter.'

example.hanzi: 古诗中常用渔樵来象征隐居生活。
example.pinyin: Gǔshī zhōng cháng yòng yúqiáo lái xiàngzhēng yǐnjū shēnghuó.
example.english: In classical poetry, 'fisherman and woodcutter' are often used to symbolize a reclusive life.
example.fact: The pairing 渔樵 (fisherman and woodcutter) recurs throughout classical Chinese poetry and painting as an idealized image of simple, self-sufficient rural life free from the pressures of court politics.

components.note: 阝 (mound/place) — on the left side, a form of 阜 (mound, earthworks), often relating to terrain, elevation, or place.
禺 (yú) gives the sound — an exact match with 隅's reading.

example.hanzi: 他独自坐在教室的一隅。
example.pinyin: Tā dúzì zuò zài jiàoshì de yì yú.
example.english: He sat alone in a corner of the classroom.
example.fact: The idiom 举一反三 ('to deduce many things from one instance') traces back to a related line from Confucius in the Analects about inferring three corners from just one.

meanings: to sieve; to sift; to filter

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — the bamboo radical, marking the character as related to bamboo or objects made of it.
师 (shī) gives a sound close to 筛's reading shāi, sharing the same initial.

example.hanzi: 公司会筛选出最合适的候选人。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī huì shāixuǎn chū zuì héshì de hòuxuǎnrén.
example.english: The company will screen out the most suitable candidate.
example.fact: The Sieve of Eratosthenes, using this same idea of a 'sieve,' is one of the oldest known algorithms for finding all prime numbers up to a given limit, devised by the ancient Greek mathematician over 2,200 years ago.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — a form of 言 (speech), marking the character as related to talking or language.
曷 (hé) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer closely matches 谒's reading yè.

example.hanzi: 游客们前来拜谒中山陵。
example.pinyin: Yóukèmen qiánlái bàiyè Zhōngshān Líng.
example.english: Tourists come to pay their respects at the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum.
example.fact: The Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing, completed in 1929, remains one of China's most visited memorial sites, honoring the founding father of the Republic of China.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the person radical, marking the character as describing a person, their role, or their behavior.
委 (wěi) gives a sound close to 倭's reading wō, sharing the same initial.

example.hanzi: 明朝时期，倭寇经常侵扰东南沿海。
example.pinyin: Míngcháo shíqī, wōkòu jīngcháng qīnrǎo dōngnán yánhǎi.
example.english: During the Ming dynasty, wokou pirates frequently raided the southeastern coast.
example.fact: 'Wokou' raiders, a mix of Japanese, Chinese, and other origins, plagued the coasts of China and Korea especially in the 14th-16th centuries, prompting massive Ming-dynasty coastal defenses under generals like Qi Jiguang.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — the sickness radical, depicting a person lying on a sickbed — marking the character as related to illness.
畀 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 痹's reading.

example.hanzi: 他的手因受伤而麻痹了。
example.pinyin: Tā de shǒu yīn shòushāng ér mábì le.
example.english: His hand became numb due to the injury.
example.fact: 麻痹大意 ('numbly careless') is a common Chinese idiom warning against complacency, often seen in workplace safety slogans reminding people not to let vigilance lapse.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — the dog/animal radical, marking the character as related to an animal.
昌 (chāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 猖's reading.

example.hanzi: 近年来网络诈骗十分猖獗。
example.pinyin: Jìnnián lái wǎngluò zhàpiàn shífēn chāngjué.
example.english: In recent years, online scams have become extremely rampant.
example.fact: 猖獗 is a common word in Chinese news reporting on crime or disease outbreaks — it always implies something spreading dangerously out of control.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the person radical, marking the character as describing a person, their role, or their behavior.
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 佯's reading.

example.hanzi: 他佯装什么都不知道。
example.pinyin: Tā yángzhuāng shénme dōu bù zhīdào.
example.english: He pretended not to know anything at all.
example.fact: The classical military strategy 声东击西 ('feinting east while attacking west') relies on the same idea as 佯攻 ('feint attack'), a tactic described in Sun Tzu's Art of War over 2,000 years ago.

meanings: used in 脫疘|脱肛[tuo1 gang1]

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — a form of 肉 (flesh, body), marking the character as related to a body part or bodily substance.
工 (gōng) gives a sound close to 肛's reading gāng, sharing the same initial and nasal ending.

example.hanzi: 医生建议他去检查一下肛门健康。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā qù jiǎnchá yíxià gāngmén jiànkāng.
example.english: The doctor advised him to get a checkup on his anal health.
example.fact: Colorectal cancer screening guidelines in many countries recommend regular colonoscopies starting around age 45-50, since early detection through such screening dramatically improves survival rates.

components.note: 爫 is a form of 爪 (hand, claw), showing a hand grasping something.

大 here represents a person; combined with a hand gripping a cord leading this figure, the character originally depicted a captive being led — giving 奚 its early meaning 'servant, slave.' Its modern use as 'where, what, why' arose later through phonetic borrowing.

example.hanzi: 奚是一个较少见的中国姓氏。
example.pinyin: Xī shì yí gè jiào shǎojiàn de Zhōngguó xìngshì.
example.english: Xi is a relatively uncommon Chinese surname.
example.fact: In classical Chinese, 奚 also functioned as an interrogative meaning 'what, why, or where' — used, for instance, in the Zhuangzi's famous story of the giant bird Peng, asking rhetorically why it needed to fly so far south.

meanings: contracted form of 不用[bu4 yong4]
etymologyHint: Not 不 needed 用; 用 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 不 means 'not.'
用 means 'to use, need.' 甭 is a 'blended-sound' character: it fuses both the meaning and, roughly, the pronunciation of 不 (bù) + 用 (yòng) into the single syllable béng, meaning 'there's no need to.'

example.hanzi: 你甭担心，一切都会好的。
example.pinyin: Nǐ béng dānxīn, yīqiè dōu huì hǎo de.
example.english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
example.fact: 甭 belongs to a small class of Chinese 'blended-sound characters,' created by fusing both the meaning and pronunciation of two existing words — here, 不 (bù, 'not') and 用 (yòng, 'need') combine into the single syllable béng.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the hand radical, marking the character as related to an action performed with the hand.
平 (píng) gives a sound close to 抨's reading pēng, sharing the same initial and nasal ending.

example.hanzi: 媒体纷纷抨击这项政策。
example.pinyin: Méitǐ fēnfēn pēngjī zhè xiàng zhèngcè.
example.english: The media sharply criticized this policy one after another.
example.fact: 抨击 is one of the most common verbs in Chinese news writing for describing strong public or media criticism, frequently paired with words like 政策 (policy) or 言论 (statements).

components.note: 虫 (insect) — the insect radical, originally depicting a snake-like shape, marking the character as related to insects or small creatures.
我 (wǒ) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer closely matches 蛾's reading é.

example.hanzi: 飞蛾在灯光下飞来飞去。
example.pinyin: Fēi'é zài dēngguāng xià fēilái fēiqù.
example.english: Moths fly back and forth under the lamplight.
example.fact: The idiom 飞蛾扑火 ('a moth flying into the flame') describes reckless self-destruction, referencing moths' well-documented attraction to artificial light, a behavior called phototaxis.

meanings: used in 嘮叨|唠叨[lao2 dao5]

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the mouth radical, marking the character as related to speech, sound, or an action of the mouth.
劳 (láo) gives the sound — an exact match with 唠's reading.

example.hanzi: 妈妈总是唠叨个不停。
example.pinyin: Māma zǒngshì láodao gè bù tíng.
example.english: Mom is always nagging nonstop.
example.fact: 唠叨 is a common Chinese word used affectionately, or with mild exasperation, to describe a parent's repeated, well-meaning reminders — a nearly universal cross-cultural experience captured in one word.

components.note: 火 (fire) — the fire radical, marking the character as related to fire, heat, or burning.

example.hanzi: 这块手表的指针会发出荧光。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài shǒubiǎo de zhǐzhēn huì fāchū yíngguāng.
example.english: The hands of this watch give off a fluorescent glow.
example.fact: Fluorescent materials absorb higher-energy light, often invisible UV, and re-emit it at a lower-energy, visible wavelength — the same principle behind fluorescent lightbulbs, highlighter ink, and glow-in-the-dark stars.
